supplementary_sources_collected.source: Tatum, J. — Chapter 3: Dipole and Quadrupole Moments (University of Victoria)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: Classical electrodynamics foundation for dipole-toroidal model; τ = p × E is the exact mechanism by which Earth's dipole field interacts with the ionospheric cavity; polarizability α explains neural tissue response to ELF fields (SR-005 mechanism)

Cortical layers show distinct oscillation patterns: gamma (fast) at surface, alpha/beta (slow) in deep layers — universal across 14 cortical areas and 4 mammalian species including humans; validates SR-002 cross-substrate match between geophysical and neural oscillations; FLIP algorithm identifies Layer 4 via frequency crossover
key_findings: Superficial layers: gamma 40-60 Hz (external sensory information)
Deep layers: alpha 6-16 Hz (internal cognitive states)
Layer 4: frequency crossover point (feedforward input hub)
Imbalances linked to ADHD (gamma dominance) and schizophrenia (alpha dominance)

supplementary_sources_collected.source: Stoupel, E. — Effect of geomagnetic activity on cardiovascular parameters (1999)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: Review of 20 years of studies: high GMA → more MI admissions, higher BP, more severe migraine, more CVA; low GMA → more sudden deaths, ventricular arrhythmias; validates SR-006
key_findings: High GMA: more acute MI, anterior wall MI, higher outpatient mortality
High GMA: higher diastolic BP, more severe migraine, more CVA admissions
Low GMA: more sudden deaths, ventricular tachycardia, inferior wall MI
Serotonergic system activation suggested as mechanism

supplementary_sources_collected.source: PMC9233046 — Geomagnetic disturbances reduce heart rate variability (2022)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: Intense GMD (Kp > 75th percentile) significantly reduces r-MSSD (-14.7ms) and SDNN (-8.2ms) up to 24h prior; stronger effect in CHD patients; validates SR-004
key_findings: Greatest HRV reduction during 0-15 hour moving average
Associations remain after adjusting for air pollutants

supplementary_sources_collected.source: PMC5805718 — Long-Term Study of HRV Responses to Solar and Geomagnetic Environment (Alabdulgader 2018)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: 5-week longitudinal study: HRV positively correlated with sunspot number, solar radio flux; validates SR-004 with temporal granularity
key_findings: IBIs positively correlated with sunspots hours 12-15 (Z 3.42-3.84, p<0.05-0.01)
TP significant at hour 10 and hours 12-15 (Z 3.25-3.73, p<0.05-0.01)
HF positively correlated hours 10-15 (Z 3.28-4.13, p<0.05-0.01)
Solar wind speed not correlated with HRV variables

supplementary_sources_collected.source: PMC3131344 — Laminar differences in gamma and alpha coherence (Buffalo 2011)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: Superficial layers show strong gamma 40-60 Hz coherence; deep layers show alpha 10 Hz peak; attention enhances gamma in superficial, reduces alpha in deep; validates laminar frequency segregation
key_findings: Superficial SFC: gamma peak 40-60 Hz, no alpha peak
Deep SFC: alpha peak ~10 Hz, minimal gamma
Attention enhances superficial gamma (V2, V4: p<0.05-0.001)
Attention reduces deep alpha (V2: median 5% decrease, V4: median 10% decrease)

supplementary_sources_collected.source: PNAS 2014 — Alpha and gamma oscillations characterize feedback and feedforward processing (Bastos et al.)
supplementary_sources_collected.relevance: Alpha propagates top-down (feedback), gamma propagates bottom-up (feedforward); gamma starts in Layer 4, propagates to superficial/deep with 1-2ms phase delay; validates information flow architecture
key_findings: Alpha: top-down propagation (feedback processing)
Gamma: bottom-up propagation starting Layer 4 (feedforward)
Gamma phase delay: 1ms deep, 2ms superficial
Pattern invariant across stimulus conditions
